result.title: RAID: Representation Autoencoder for Intrinsic Decomposition
result.summary: Single-image intrinsic decomposition is an inherently ill-posed problem, requiring the disentanglement of strongly coupled appearance factors from a single RGB observation. Recent methods address this ambiguity with diffusion priors, at the cost of large, iterative, and often stochastic models. We show that accurate decomposition does not require a large generative model. Our key idea is to decouple reconstruction from decomposition on top of a strong pretrained representation. First, an $X \rightarrow X$ teacher learns to reconstruct each intrinsic map from DINOv3 features using a shared decoder, without paired RGB-to-intrinsic supervision. Then, a DINOv3-based student predicts the corresponding teacher representations from RGB through lightweight, modality-specific projections, enabling training on partially annotated datasets and predicting all intrinsics in a single forward pass. \textbf{RAID}, predicts intrinsic properties in the structured latent space, enabling a compact 165M-parameter model, 100x faster than diffusion-based methods. Despite its compact size, it achieves competitive or superior decomposition quality, with improved robustness to input resolution. Additionally, our learned projections yield interpretable, modality-specific feature spaces.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RAID，在 DINOv3 预训练表示上先由 X→X 教师学习重建各 intrinsic map，再由学生用轻量模态投影从 RGB 预测对应表示，实现单次前向的本征分解，模型仅 165M 参数。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作是纯视觉的本征图像分解，目标是把外观因素解耦为可重建的稠密图，不涉及推理状态生成、视觉证据筛选、动态计算或停止决策，与 LVR 主线缺少具体可借用的机制线索；其表示空间解耦虽与潜在状态保真略有形式相似，但停留在像素级外观因子上，不足以构成迁移依据。
